card.statement: Notice that, depending on the choice of the fiber functor $\mathcal{F}$, the prestack $\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}$ may be a stack on $(\mathsf{Aff}/X,\mathrm{fppf})$. This is the case for example if $\mathcal{F}$ is representable, or if $\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}\smallsetminus Z}$ for $Z\subset X$ a closed subscheme (see [9, Proposition 2.6.2], and [10, Theorem 7.8] for the affine case). In general, we do not know whether, for arbitrary $X$, $D$ and $Z$, all the different $\mathbf{Bun}_{\mathcal{F}}$ appearing in the Grassmannians of Definition 2.10 are étale or fppf stacks. We also remark that the same problem would arise by considering the derived version $\mathbb{R}\mathsf{Bun}$ of $\mathsf{Bun}$ and derived completions instead of the classical completions considered throughout the paper.
card.label: Remark 2.11

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
